title: mu settings
description: Everything mu can be told: judges, decision points, features, models and context. Shared with the mu command line.
applyNote: Changes apply to new sessions. A running session keeps the configuration it started with; reconnect it to pick them up.
keyHelp: Once saved it is never shown again. It stays on this computer, readable only by your account.
keyKeep: Leave empty to keep the saved key
endpointRule: Use HTTPS, or HTTP to this machine only (127.0.0.1, localhost). No user name, password, query or fragment in the address.

modes.offHelp: The verdict has no effect: that step goes ahead as usual.

harness.tooOld: This version of mu is too old to list its decision points and features. Update mu to see them here; the basic settings still work.
harness.unsupported: mu describes itself in a format this app does not know (version {{version}}). Update the app to edit decision points and features.

load.failed: The settings could not be loaded

save.saved: Saved. New sessions use it; reconnect running ones.
save.stale: Another program (the mu command line, or a running session) changed the configuration after it was loaded here, so nothing was saved. Reload to see the current state; your unsaved edits will be lost.

options.addNumber: Type a number and press Enter

problem.type: This value has the wrong type.
problem.range: This value is outside the allowed range.
problem.choice: This is not one of the choices.
problem.length: Too long, or an entry is empty.

decisions.description: Each point where the judge is asked. A point follows the default mode unless you give it one of its own.
decisions.defaultModeHelp: For every decision point without a mode of its own.
decisions.featureOff: Its feature is off, so this point is not asked now.
decisions.pageLead: A point follows the default mode unless you give it one of its own. The default mode and the search are on {{page}}.

features.lead: What mu does for you in the background. Switch one off and mu stops doing it.
features.moreLead: Everything else mu can do, grouped by where it acts. Each feature’s options are one click away.
features.boardModelElsewhere: The model that writes the board is chosen under Default model.
features.noOptions: Nothing else to set: the switch is all there is.
features.noSuchFeature: This version of mu has no such feature.

judges.tiersHelp: Judges are tried in order. A later one only sees what the earlier ones left uncertain.
judges.orderHelp: The first one is the judge chosen above.
judges.baseUrlHelp: Leave empty to use TypeSafe's own address.
judges.customTier: A judge you added yourself. Change it in mu's settings file.

types.jevHelp: TypeSafe directly when its key is set, otherwise the Vercel AI Gateway.
types.gatewayHelp: Always through the Vercel AI Gateway.

judges.intro: While it works, mu makes many small calls: how to handle this message, whether this step breaks a rule you set. The judge answers them. Pick one.
judges.custom: The first judge right now is a custom one: see and change it under Judge tiers below.
judges.keyPlaceholder: Paste a TypeSafe or Vercel AI Gateway key

jev.title: Jev
jev.description: Fast and accurate, billed per call. Needs a TypeSafe or Vercel AI Gateway key.

local.title: Local Laya
local.description: Runs on this computer, no network, no cost. Good at classifying; relating and scoring are less reliable.

laya.stopped: Installed, not running. mu starts it when it needs it.
laya.platform: Laya cannot run on this computer: it needs Windows or Linux (x64 or arm64) or a Mac with Apple Silicon.
laya.needsUv: Installing needs uv, a Python package manager. Install it, then come back here.
laya.confirmText: This downloads about {{size}} MB from PyPI and Hugging Face (Python packages and the model's weights) into mu's folder, and takes a few minutes. Laya starts once it is installed.

failed.setup: Installing did not finish. You can try again.

onnx.missing: Laya's model is not on this computer yet (about {{size}} MB). mu does not download it for you: get the files from Hugging Face, put them in the model folder, then press Check and start.
onnx.stopped: The model is in place, and Laya is not running. When Laya is your judge, mu starts it by itself when the app opens.
onnx.starting: Checking the model and starting Laya… The first check reads the whole model and takes a moment.
onnx.wrongFiles: Not the version mu was tested with, download these again: {{files}}
onnx.command: With the Hugging Face command line (hf), this one command fetches everything:

problem.wrong: Some model files are not the version mu was tested with. Download them again.
problem.runtime: This computer could not run the model.
problem.port: Another program already uses Laya's port ({{port}}).
problem.stopped: Laya stopped before it was ready.
problem.foreign: A Laya that mu did not start is running here. Stop it where it was started.

context.autoHelp: Compacts the history when the context is nearly full.
context.limitHelp: 0 follows the model's window minus the reserve. Otherwise {{min}} to {{max}}. Checked before the next model request; not a hard cut.
context.limitProblem: Use 0, or a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.
context.lead: When the conversation is compacted, how large its context may grow, and the decision points about context.

kind.edit: mu wants to edit a file
kind.shell: mu wants to run a command
kind.run: mu wants to run a program
kind.outside: mu wants to change a file outside the project

reason.ask: Minimal permissions: every step asks you first.
reason.unsure: Jev is not sure this step is what you want.
reason.beyond: Jev thinks this goes beyond what you asked for.
reason.unrelated: Jev thinks this is not part of the task.
reason.protected: This touches mu’s own settings; only you can allow it.

providers.lead: Where the models come from: subscriptions and endpoints. A conversation’s model and thinking level are picked in its send box.
providers.title: Providers
providers.name: Display name
providers.idHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It cannot change once saved.

idProblem.format: Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit (at most 40).
idProblem.reserved: This is the id of a built-in provider. An entry under it would reroute that provider instead of adding one.
idProblem.taken: This id is already in use.

providers.keyReplace: A key written by hand is in use. Typing one here replaces it.
providers.authHeader: Also send Authorization: Bearer (some proxies need it)
providers.headers: Extra headers written by hand are kept as they are: {{names}}. Their values are secrets and are edited in models.json.
providers.pick: Choose a provider on the left, or add one.
providers.foreignHelp: This entry reroutes a built-in provider, or uses an API format this screen does not edit. It can be removed here but not edited: edit it in models.json.
providers.builtinHelp: mu reported it as usable at its last connection, usually because its API key is in the environment. It cannot be removed here: delete that key from the environment, and it is gone after mu connects again.
providers.unreadable: models.json could not be read, so providers are neither shown nor saved. Repair it by hand, then reload.
providers.commented: models.json contains comments. Saving from here would remove them, so providers are read-only. Remove the comments by hand to edit here.
providers.summary: Sign in with a subscription and use it right away, or connect any OpenAI-, Anthropic- or Gemini-compatible endpoint.
providers.removeSaved: When you save, it is deleted from models.json, and so is the key stored for it.
providers.removeUnsaved: It is not saved yet, so what you filled in here is discarded.
providers.removeEntry: When you save, this hand-written entry is deleted from models.json. If it overrides a built-in provider, that provider goes back to its defaults.
providers.removeDefault: New sessions start with it, so the default model is cleared too.

defaults.summary: What a new session starts with. You can still switch inside a conversation.
defaults.levelHelp: Levels this model does not take are disabled.
defaults.levelClamped: Not set means medium. A level the model does not take becomes the nearest one it does.
defaults.noReasoning: This model does not think, so a session with it always starts with thinking off.

accounts.signOutFailed: Signing out did not finish. You can try again.
accounts.signOutConfirm: Sign out of {{name}}? You will need to sign in again to use it.
accounts.instant: Signing in and out takes effect at once, without saving.
accounts.byKeyHelp: No subscription is signed in, but mu reported it as usable at its last connection, usually because its API key is in the environment. Signing in switches it to the subscription.
accounts.otherRunning: {{name}} is signing in, and one sign-in runs at a time.

models.idField: Model ID · as the API expects it

boardModel.title: Plain-language model
boardModel.summary: Writes the plain-language board: how the work is going, in everyday words. For you only, never in the conversation’s context; each update is one call.
boardModel.recommended: Recommended: Claude Opus 4.6, the most natural and steady; then Gemini 3.8 Flash, faster and cheaper.
boardModel.unset: None yet: mu asks the first time the board is switched on.
boardModel.sessionHelp: When the conversation switches model, the board follows.
boardModel.update: This version of mu cannot be told here which model writes the board. Update mu first.

judge.title: Choose a judge
judge.subtitle: The judge answers the small calls mu makes while it works. mu runs without one, just without these checks.

done.title: All set
done.subtitle: Check it over, then start.
done.noKey: No key yet: judgments follow the default rules until there is one

intro.title: Welcome to mu
intro.lead: mu is a coding assistant that does the work: it reads your project, edits code, runs commands and tests, and keeps going until the job is done.

judge.title: A check at every step
judge.text: A built-in judge watches the key moments: think before acting, keep to the rules you set, never call it done unverified.

control.title: You see it, you steer it
control.text: Any change can be rolled back; every step in the browser is in view, and you can pause or take over.

ready.title: Ready out of the box
ready.text: It picks up the rules, skills and MCP servers you already set up in Claude Code, Cursor and Codex.

login.waiting: The {{name}} sign-in page is open in your browser. Sign in and allow access; this continues by itself.
login.codePlaceholder: Paste the code the browser shows, or the address it ended on
login.failed: Signing in did not finish. You can try again.
login.needAccount: Sign in to an account first, then pick a model.
login.waitingDevice: The {{name}} verification page is open in your browser. Check that the code there matches this one (type it in if it is not filled in), approve, and this continues by itself.

risk.title: Know the risk before you sign in
risk.text: This signs in through the login Google made for {{tool}} itself, not one Google provides for mu. Google may treat that as against its terms and limit or suspend the account.
risk.instead: Use an account you can afford to lose access to. The official ways are a Gemini API key, or Vertex AI signed in with gcloud.
risk.continue: I understand the risk, sign in

login.readingModels: Signed in to {{name}}. Reading the models this account can use…

turnErrors.processExited: mu stopped in the middle of the turn. Send the message again to restart it.
turnErrors.turnRunning: mu is still working on the previous message. Wait for it, or stop it first.
turnErrors.busyConfig: Wait for the current turn to finish before changing the model or thinking level.
turnErrors.unsupportedValue: mu does not offer this model, thinking level or permission mode.
turnErrors.permissionsNotSwitched: mu did not switch the permission mode. Try again, or type /permissions in the conversation.
turnErrors.imageUnsupported: Only PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF images up to 12 MB can be sent.
turnErrors.contentUnsupported: mu accepts only text, images and text files.
turnErrors.wrongProject: This conversation belongs to another project folder.
turnErrors.notPersisted: mu could not save this conversation.
turnErrors.timeout: mu did not answer in time.
turnErrors.processClosed: mu has stopped. Send the message again to restart it.

notices.answerLost: mu did not get your answer, so it went on as if you had declined.
notices.bashMissing: mu needs Git for Windows to run commands. Once it is installed, send your message again. Download it here:

errors.credential: The key contains characters a key cannot have, such as spaces, quotes or line breaks. Paste it again.
errors.keyVariable: {{name}} cannot hold a judge key. Use TYPESAFE_API_KEY, AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, or a name that starts with MU_JUDGE_.
errors.sharedKey: {{providers}} would share one key variable. Change one of the IDs.
errors.pickBoth: Choose a provider and a model together.
errors.modelsUnreadable: models.json could not be read. Repair it by hand before saving providers.
errors.modelsCommented: models.json contains comments, which saving from here would remove. Edit providers by hand.

errors.runtimeOffline: The mu runtime is not online. Check the local launcher and the sign-in.
